slides.title: The Third Dimension 🌌
slides.content:
# Going Beyond 2D

CSS can simulate 3D space with `rotateX()`, `rotateY()`, `rotateZ()`, and `translateZ()`. These require a **perspective** to give the illusion of depth.

3D transforms affect how elements are rendered, not the actual DOM. The browser calculates them using matrix3d.

slides.title: Perspective Origin & `transform-style` 🎚️
slides.content:
# Fine‑Tuning 3D Space

- `perspective-origin` – where the viewer is looking from (default centre). e.g., `perspective-origin: left top;`
- `transform-style: preserve-3d;` – allows children to exist in 3D space. Otherwise, they flatten onto the parent's plane.

These properties enable complex 3D scenes.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Test on Real Devices

3D transforms can be heavy on mobile GPUs. Use `will-change: transform;` to optimise, but don't overuse it.
